title: Copper: Cooperative Caching Layer for Scalable Data Loading in Exascale Supercomputers
problem: Job initialization time increases significantly as HPC jobs scale to larger node counts because processes flood the storage system with redundant I/O requests for the same files, causing nodes to remain idle and wasting CPU cycles.
motivation: Eliminating I/O bottlenecks at job initialization is critical for achieving efficient data loading on exascale supercomputers with thousands of nodes.
method: Copper implements a read-only cooperative caching layer that coordinates data loading across multiple nodes to prevent storage flooding. The cache is shared cooperatively so that multiple processes access previously-loaded data through the cache rather than redundantly requesting from storage, reducing storage-side congestion.
key_novelty: A cooperative caching mechanism that maintains near-constant load time when scaling from 32 to 8,300 nodes by coordinating data access across the entire job.
contributions: Copper cooperative caching layer design for scalable data loading
Near-constant load time demonstrated across 217x scale range (32 to 8,300 nodes)
Elimination of storage I/O congestion during parallel job initialization
Evaluation and validation on production Aurora supercomputer
